title: A vacation in Georgia
goal: Tell the story of a trip from start to finish, praise and complain about places, and bring together everything you've learned in one complete story.
bekal: tell the story of a trip in a clear order
praise a place with more than one adjective
name regions and famous places in Georgia
link sentences with მერე, შემდეგ, ბოლოს

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — A week in Kakheti and Batumi
dialogs.intro: Ani has just come back from a week-long trip and tells her teacher about it. Every tool she uses in this dialogue is one you already have — the past from unit 17, place endings from unit 7, comparisons from unit 14.

lines.speaker: გიორგი:
lines.id: Ani, where were you last week?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: I was in Kakheti and Batumi. I traveled for a week.
lines.literal: Kakheti-and — and — Batumi-in — I-was. one — week — I-traveled.

lines.speaker: გიორგი:
lines.id: How was it? What did you see?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: First I went to Sighnaghi. It's a small town, but really beautiful.
lines.literal: first — Sighnaghi-in — I-went. small — town-is, but — very — beautiful.

lines.speaker: გიორგი:
lines.id: Did you see a wine cellar?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Yes! I saw a qvevri too. I didn't know wine was aged in the ground.
lines.literal: yes! qvevri-too — I-saw. not — I-knew, that — wine — ground-in — ripens.

lines.speaker: გიორგი:
lines.id: It's been done that way for eight thousand years. And then?
lines.literal: eight — thousand — year-is — so — is-made. then?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Then I took the train to Batumi. I saw the Black Sea for the first time.
lines.literal: then — train-by — Batumi-in — I-went-down. for-the-first-time — I-saw — black — sea.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: No! It's different. Batumi is warm and lively, but Tbilisi is my home.
lines.literal: no! different-is. Batumi — warm-is — and — noisy, Tbilisi — though — my — home-is.

lines.speaker: გიორგი:
lines.id: You put that nicely, Ani. Did anything bad happen?
lines.literal: this — well — you-said, Ani. bad — something — happened?

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: It rained on the last day and I left my bag at the hotel. Everything else was fine.
lines.literal: last — day-on — it-rained — and — bag — got-forgotten-by-me — hotel-in. other — everything — well — was.

notes: **A story is built with three linking words: ჯერ (first), მერე / შემდეგ (then), ბოლოს (finally).** These three words turn a pile of sentences into a story. Add **პირველად** (for the first time) and your story instantly has weight.

**დამავიწყდა = "it got forgotten by me".** ⚠️ Georgian doesn't say "I forgot" — it's not the person who forgets, but the thing that "slips away" from the person. The form is reversed like მტკივა: **და**მ**ავიწყდა** (I forgot), **და**გ**ავიწყდა** (you forgot). The phrase *არ დაგავიწყდეს!* from unit 8 can finally be taken apart: "don't let it get forgotten by you".
**ვიცოდი = "I knew"**, the past of ვიცი. Notice the pairing: *არ ვიცოდი, რომ…* (I didn't know that…), a very useful sentence for reacting to something new.

**რომ = "that".** The linking word that opens up all complex sentences: *ვიცი, რომ კარგია* (I know that it's good), *ვფიქრობ, რომ ძვირია* (I think that it's expensive). One small word that instantly raises your level.

**A ქვევრი (qvevri) is a large clay jar buried in the ground** and used for making wine in Georgia for eight thousand years. The method is on UNESCO's cultural heritage list, and Georgians see it as proof that their country is the birthplace of wine. If you visit Kakheti, the question *ქვევრი შემიძლია ვნახო?* will almost always get you a little tour and a free tasting.

**სხვაა = "it's different".** A tactful and very Georgian way to avoid a comparison that could offend. Saying *ბათუმი უკეთესია* in front of someone from Tbilisi — or the other way around — is no small matter.
**შავი ზღვა = the Black Sea.** Notice that even place names put the adjective first, just like the pattern in unit 11.

grammars.title: Putting a story together
after: The easiest story structure that always works: **when → where → what happened → what it was like**. *გასულ კვირას ბათუმში ვიყავი. ზღვა ვნახე. ძალიან ლამაზი იყო.* Three sentences, and that's already a story.

grammars.title: Praising and complaining
after: **მომეწონა** is the past of მომწონს (unit 10): "I liked it (back then)". A reversed verb stays reversed in the past.

blocks.text: These names will come up in every conversation about travel. Saying them correctly — especially Sakartvelo, not "Georgia" — makes your conversation stand out right away.

blocks.title: Five sentences for telling the story of a trip
items: **გასულ კვირას ბათუმში ვიყავი.** — I was in Batumi last week.
**პირველად ვნახე ზღვა.** — I saw the sea for the first time.

blocks.text: If you're looking for a first trip to try, almost every Georgian will suggest the same thing: **მცხეთა** for a day, because it's close and explains a lot about the country's history; then **კახეთი** for a weekend, because that's where wine, the supra, and Georgian hospitality are at their fullest.

exercises.prompt: Order the story with the right linking word.
Put the words in the right order.

items: I was in Kakheti last week.
It's a small town, but really beautiful.
I saw the sea for the first time.
